items.hint: Two questions before you compute anything: exactly what is the exponent attached to, and how much of what you see belongs to the denominator?
worked: No bracket holds the minus sign, so the exponent binds first: $-5^{2}=-(5^{2})=-25$.
Everything written under the bar is one grouped denominator: $\dfrac{18}{3+6}=\dfrac{18}{9}=2$.

items.stem: Exactly one of the four statements below is true. Which statement is true?
items.hint: Finish whatever sits inside a grouping symbol before you divide or take a root; a fraction bar and a radical each act like invisible parentheses.
worked: The bar groups the whole numerator, so $\dfrac{9+3}{3}=\dfrac{12}{3}=4$. The $3$'s cannot be cancelled, because $9+3$ is a sum and only whole factors cancel.
$\dfrac{20}{4+1}=\dfrac{20}{5}=4$, not $25$. Test the splitting idea on easy numbers: $\dfrac{1}{1+1}=\dfrac{1}{2}$, but $\dfrac{1}{1}+\dfrac{1}{1}=2$.
$\sqrt{25+144}=\sqrt{169}=13$, not $17$; the radical groups everything underneath it, so the sum happens first.

items.hint: There are three grouped pieces here; work each one out completely on its own line, then combine the three numbers left to right.
worked: The radical groups the sum beneath it: $\sqrt{36+64}=\sqrt{100}=10$.
